Surprisingly decent Fall Guys clone. I bought Fall Guys on day 1 for full price, and enjoyed playing it on Linux until they added EasyAntiCheat, after which the game would not launch. Even now that EAC is supported through Proton, Fall Guys will launch but I have EAC related error messages. I contacted support and they only offered useless Windows workarounds while stating that the game isn't supported on Linux. Pain in the ass, hours wasted on troubleshooting. Then along comes Stumble Guys to save the day! It runs on Linux no problem. The gameplay is solid, perhaps a little bit too basic -- you can move, and jump, and if you tap jump again in the air you dive forward. There is no grabbing ledges and players like in Fall Guys, for better or worse. The audio is pretty awful -- the music is annoying and repetitive, and doesn't even loop properly, I muted it within ten minutes of playing. This exposes the very sparse sound effects -- no footsteps, all you can hear is your own jump and cannons firing. That's the worst of it though, otherwise the gameplay is enjoyable.

Heart-gripping, blood-pumping action knocks you off of your feet and down into its deep blue void in Kitka Games' much sought after release, Stumble Guys. The furious, flamboyant and fast paced gameplay will have you on the edge of your seat throughout its duration as you jump, slide, and taunt your way to the ends of each level, barely scraping your way into the next event. This isn't a game of teams and long thought strategy, it's a hardcore and competitive experience in which all it equips you with are your hard-earned gamer skills and reflexes, not to mention the whimsical boops and bops of its beautifully composed soundtrack. Beware of yourself and your surroundings as you compete in this massively multiplayer competitive esport action roleplaying videogame, for when you Stumble, you are also bound to Tumble.

Overall, we rate Stumble Guys a strong and heartfelt 9.32/10.
